turns.t: Well, doctor, you know how it is, I came in last month about my back and now there's a new thing, a numb patch on my thigh.
Right, let's look at the new thing first. Which thigh, and where exactly?
The left one, on the outside. About the size of my palm. It feels like it's been to the dentist.
When did you first notice it?
Oh, a few weeks ago? Maybe longer, my daughter thinks it was when we went on holiday. I honestly couldn't say.
Is it getting bigger, or staying the same?
Staying the same, I think.
Any weakness in the leg, or pain going down from your back?
No weakness. No pain in the leg at all.
Any problems passing water or opening your bowels?
No, nothing at all in that department.
How has your back been since the last visit? ~
Much better, thank you. The physio helped. ~
Good. What medicines are you taking now?
Naproxen, 500 mg, twice a day, with food. And a tablet for the nerves, amitriptyline, 10 mg, at night. Or was it 25? My wife has the box.
We'll check the dose on the box next time. Any other medical conditions?
Diabetes, for six years. High blood pressure. And I had a slipped disc some years ago.
Thank you. Do you smoke?
Used to. I gave up fifteen years ago.
Let me check your pulse and pressure first. ~
Go on.
Pulse 76, blood pressure 138 over 84.
Is that fine? ~
Reasonable. Now I'd like to touch the patch on your thigh with a cotton wool and a pin. Tell me what you feel. ~
All right.
There is reduced sensation to light touch and pinprick over the outer left thigh, and the rest of the leg is normal.
What does that mean? ~
It's a pattern we see when a small skin nerve is squeezed, often called meralgia paraesthetica. Diabetes can make it more likely.
Is it serious? ~
It isn't dangerous, and it often settles. I'd like to check your blood sugar and your B12 with a blood test.
Fine. ~
Avoid tight belts and trousers, and I'll ask the physio to look at it too.
Thank you, doctor. ~
